# Log golden fixtures

Generated by `src/backend/logger/__tests__/logGolden.test.ts` from the unmodified TypeScript logger
(`LogWriter`, `formatLogMessage`, `sanitizeRendererLogMessage`) before any Phase 84 logger change. The
oracle test owns these bytes, and the directory is prettier-ignored for that reason (same rule as
`ipcSchemaSnapshot.json`). Plan 84-07 deletes the TS oracle; the fixtures stay and the Rust writer
(`gamelib-log`) and the TS forwarder are held to them.

## Files

- `cases.json`: the inputs. A JSON array of `GoldenCase` (the type is documented at the top of the test).
  Kinds: `line` (one `LogWriter.logDebug|logInfo|logWarning|logError` call), `chunks` (raw `writeString`
  chunks), `rotate` (ordered writer instances over a pre-existing file), `close` (chunks, `close()`, then a
  write that must throw), `renderer` (a renderer `logError`/`logInfo` send: sanitised, then written with the
  Frontend prefix). `{"$gen": {"repeat": "a", "count": 65537}}` inside a message or value expands to a
  string of that length. A case with `"oracle": false` is hand-written (see below).
- `expected/<id>/<relative path>`: every file the oracle produced for the case, `.old` included. A case that
  writes no file (a disabled writer, an empty message) has no directory, because git cannot hold an empty one.
- `entries.json`: per oracle case, the frame entries the new forwarder must emit. Shape per case:
  `{ id, frames: [ { target, rotate, entries: [ {line: {ts, tz, level, prefix, msg}} | {raw} ] } ] }`, or
  `{ id, renderer: { channel, value } }` for renderer cases (the Rust side applies the sanitiser).
  `prefix` is the `LogPrefix` value (empty string for General) and `msg` is the formatted line with its
  prefix chunk removed. One frame per writer instance; `rotate` is true when that instance's first accepted
  entry arrives (a non-general instance only; general entries never carry `rotate`, because Rust rotates
  `gamelib.log` once per app launch). An accepted entry that produces no line (an empty message) still claims
  the rotation, so its frame has `rotate: true` and no entries.
- Token `${LOGDIR}` stands for the temp root the case ran in (a log directory root). It appears in file
  contents, for example the `Logging to file(s) ${LOGDIR}/games/480_steam/launch.log` line. A `gogRedist`
  target resolves to `${LOGDIR}/userData/GamesConfig/gog-redist.log` (D-20).

## Regenerating

```sh
GAMELIB_WRITE_LOG_GOLDEN=1 pnpm exec jest --runTestsByPath src/backend/logger/__tests__/logGolden.test.ts
```

Without the variable the test is in compare mode: it regenerates everything in memory and asserts every
expected file, `entries.json` and the set of case directories match exactly. Review the diff of a regeneration
by hand; a changed byte in `expected/` is a behaviour change.

## Time and timezone

Every case runs at a fake wall-clock instant of 2026-11-20 13:05:09 local time, so every line starts
`(13:05:09)` on any host. `entries.json` records `ts` (epoch milliseconds) and `tz` (minutes east of UTC,
`-new Date(ts).getTimezoneOffset()`) from the host that generated it. Consumers compare wall-clock time,
`ts + tz * 60000`, so the fixtures are host-timezone independent.

## File mode is not part of the golden

D-18: the TS writer's `appendFile` and `mkdir` never set a mode, so today's files are `0o666 & ~umask`. The
Rust writer deliberately creates log files 0600 on unix. That is pinned by a separate unix test in
`gamelib-log`, not by this tree.

## The hand-written case

`shell-line` has `"oracle": false`: a Rust-originated `[Shell]` INFO line, `reaper started (pid 4242)`. TS has
no `Shell` prefix, so no oracle can produce it. Its expectation was written by hand from 84-CONTEXT D-01 with
the padding computed from `constants.ts` (`[Shell]:` padded to 18, the longest prefix being 15 characters). The
case carries a `divergenceNote` naming that source, and the oracle test only checks that its files exist.
(`src-tauri/crates/README.md` section 6: new cases are written by hand with a Rust-verified value and a note.)

## Deliberate behaviour changes the Rust side pins with its own tests

These are not in the golden because the TS writer does the opposite:

1. `gamelib.log` rotates once per app launch, not once per sidecar process.
2. A second GameLib launch never rotates or initialises the writer.
3. An empty `XDG_STATE_HOME` or `LOCALAPPDATA` is treated as unset (TS uses `??`, so an empty string is "set").
4. A failed rotation rename (a Windows `.old` held open elsewhere) keeps appending instead of dropping the line.
5. A single log message over the per-entry cap is truncated with a marker.
6. New files are created 0600 on unix.

## The oracle was deleted in 84-07

The TS oracle (`logGolden.test.ts`) was deleted in Phase 84 plan 07 together with the TS writer it drove
(`log_writer.ts`, `formatter.ts`, `paths.ts`). The fixtures in this directory stay: `cases.json`,
`entries.json`, `expected/` and this file are what the Rust golden (`cargo test -p gamelib-log --test golden`)
keeps asserting against, and `src/backend/__tests__/loggerPortComplete.test.ts` fails if they go. With no
oracle left, new cases are written by hand with a Rust-verified value and a note
(`src-tauri/crates/README.md` section 6), as `shell-line` was.
